So Leo has been shaking his head a lot the last few days, the owner says both ears look red and there is a brownish discharge, he scratches the left one more than the right. He is a three-and-a-half-year-old neutered male Labrador, indoor-outdoor, swims in the canal behind the house almost every weekend. The owner also mentions lethargy this week, he skips his morning walk, eats a bit less, otherwise still drinks normally, no vomiting, stools look normal. History: ear infection last autumn was treated with ear drops for two weeks and it cleared up, no reaction to the antibiotics then. He is on Apoquel 5.4 milligrams once daily for allergies since spring, and monthly heartworm prevention. Vaccines up to date last spring. Diet is a large-breed kibble twice a day plus dental chews, sometimes table scraps of chicken. No known drug allergy beyond the owner being unsure about penicillin. Exam today: weight twenty-four point one kilograms, temperature thirty-eight point nine degrees celsius, heart rate one hundred twenty beats per minute, respiratory rate twenty-eight breaths per minute, capillary refill time under two seconds, hydration feels good, body condition score four out of nine, pain score two out of ten. Both ear canals are erythematous with brown waxy debris, left one smells yeasty, right one less so. Eyes clear, no nasal discharge, oral mucous membranes pink with mild tartar on the upper carnassials. Lungs clear bronchovesicular sounds, heart rhythm regular without a murmur. Abdomen soft non-painful, no organomegaly appreciated, no masses in the submandibular or popliteal lymph nodes. Skin shows scattered pyoderma papules along the ventral abdomen and both elbows. Musculoskeletal gait is sound, mild crepitus of the left stifle on flexion, no cranial drawer. Neurological exam within normal limits, mentation bright. Plan discussed with the owner: ear cytology from both ears first to confirm whether we are dealing with cocci yeast or mixed organisms, then an otic preparation twice daily for fourteen days, clean the canals with the ceruminolytic solution twice a week, oral anti-itch medication stays as is unless the cytology changes the picture. Bloodwork was mentioned but the owner declines it today, we agreed to recheck weight and ears in two weeks and to send the cytology results to the owner in writing. The owner asks about swimming, we say pools and canals are off-limits until the follow-up, a cone is only needed if he digs at the canals overnight. Also talked about diet transition to a hydrolysed trial for six weeks starting next Monday, the owner will buy the two-month bag, and we will log a daily scratch score on the home worksheet. The previous bloodwork from last winter showed a packed cell volume of forty-two percent, total protein six point eight grams per deciliter, albumin three point two grams per deciliter, and a urine specific gravity of one point zero three five.
